item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is the preferable starting point because it is less invasive and explicitly verifies retrying buffered content from a non-seekable reader, but neither patch satisfies the frozen contract.","reasons":["B leaves the existing FilesOption declarations and constructors untouched, whereas A changes their public return types and introduces overlapping FilesRequestOption/UploadFileOption machinery.","B’s retry test uses io.MultiReader, directly covering the required streamed, non-replayable source case; A’s Upload retry test uses an *os.File and therefore misses that specific requirement.","B has less unrelated churn: A additionally changes RetryPolicy documentation and substantially expands retry guidance beyond the requested upload API.","Both incorrectly define Upload with ...UploadFileOption instead of the exact required ...FilesOption signature, and both call Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add."],"risks_a":["Adds forbidden association options and arbitrary multipart form fields.","Changes existing option API return types, risking source incompatibility and violating the instruction to keep FilesOption behavior unchanged.","Extends raw request replay machinery, changing Files.Add and other reader-body behavior despite the contract requiring preservation and no unrelated retry refactorings adherence to scope discipline despite passing compatibility gates. Likewise introduces NewFileWithFields instead of simply using multipartbody.NewFile as required by the contract, and Upload bypasses Add, duplicating its request/response handling and potentially diverging error semantics. Also lacks an explicit source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["Adds forbidden association fields, including project association, and a separate Upload option hierarchy.","Uses multipartbody.NewForm rather than the required NewFile helper.","Upload bypasses Add, duplicating request construction and response decoding while omitting existing FilesOption query handling.
